description: Handwritten Go change fixtures, labeled before the first model run. They test observable error handling, not general bug finding.
diff_task: a change that causes a persistent state write or rollback operation to have its failure silently ignored, where that failure was previously returned, logged, or otherwise handled
function_task: a function that silently ignores a failure from a persistent state write or rollback operation instead of returning, logging, or otherwise handling the error

cases.reason: A config write loses its error check.
The write remains assigned, but the check is deleted.
A rollback rename error becomes discarded.
A persistent history write stops logging its failure.
Deferred transaction commit loses error reporting.
The check remains syntactically but the branch no longer reports the write failure.
A wrapped durable-write error is replaced by an ignored return.
A rollback helper drops the failure returned by restore.
A new error check improves handling.
Directly returning the error preserves the removed branch's behavior.
An in-memory map deletion has no fallible persistent write.
Best-effort temporary cleanup is distinct from durable-state rollback.
Logging changes format, but still handles the write error.
A comment claims errors are ignored, but the body still propagates them.
Existing ignored error is unchanged; only the comment changes.
Renaming an argument does not introduce the existing unhandled write.
A deleted function removes the operation itself, not just error handling.
A new function checks the durable write.
The ignored error comes from rendering, not persistence or rollback.
The persistent write error is still returned through an explicit variable.
